summary: Quarterly health check focused on usage growth, rising token costs, a recent 40m outage that impacted one region, and alignment on a pilot expansion. Customer is evaluating moving some workloads to Dedicated or Private for latency guarantees and compliance. Action: pricing update, benchmarks, and security docs to support procurement.
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-10-14
Start: 16:00 PT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Carlos Rivera (Redwood SE), Jia Patel (Redwood CSM), Tom Reynolds (Atlantic Head of ML), Priya Singh (Platform Eng), Alex Moore (CTO)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick QBR / health check for Atlantic Analytics. how are folks doing?
[00:08] Tom: good, thanks, Maya. busy quarter, lots of model launches. wanted to go over usage spikes and that outage last week.
[00:15] Priya: yea we saw a pretty big cost jump month over month, was hoping to understand why tokens doubled for a few routes.
[00:23] Maya: okay great — we'll walk through usage, cost, reliability, and some options for dedicated / private. Carlos will cover the performance side.
[00:30] Carlos: hi all. quick note, first off sorry about the region incident, we traced it to a mis-scheduled autoscale job hitting the dedicated pool and a fallback mis-route that caused longer queue times. not everyone was affected but latency spiked ~3x for about 40 minutes.
[00:50] Alex: right — our support tickets showed 5xxs and timeouts which caused a batch of user requests to retry and snowballed. can you confirm root cause?
[01:00] Carlos: yes, it was a combination: a scheduled maintenance overlap on our infra layer, and a config on your side that had low max-concurrency for a high-throughput route; the fallback to the cheaper variant introduced a cold-start on KV cache. we've fixed the autoscale windows and suggested changing the route concurrency.
[01:22] Tom: okay makes sense. can you share the post-mortem?
[01:25] Jia: i'll share the incident notes and the post-mortem summary after the call — short version in the deck link we posted in chat.
[01:33] Priya: on the cost side, any visibility into why tokens jumped? we didn't change prompts that much.
[01:40] Maya: couple of things — longer outputs, some increased sampling temperature for a subset of routes, and we detected a higher average context length which increases per-token cost. also the cache hit-rate dropped around the incident window which amplified costs.
[01:55] Tom: hmm we did push a new conversational flow that returned longer summaries, that would explain it. what are recommendations to reduce cost without hurting quality?
[02:05] Carlos: we recommend: 1) tighter length limits or truncation for non-critical routes, 2) configure prefix KV caching for repeated prompts, 3) consider a quantized model variant for bulk batch jobs, and 4) use batch endpoints with a short latency SLO for non-interactive jobs.
[02:25] Priya: can you quantify cost savings? ballpark numbers help in procurement.
[02:28] Maya: yes, i'll send an updated pricing sheet with committed throughput tiers. rough example: moving 30% of inference to quantized variants + caching could cut unit cost ~40%. we'll put exact spreads in the spreadsheet.
[02:41] Alex: we're also exploring Dedicated vs Private. Dedicated gives predictable throughput, Private gives us control for compliance. any recommendations?
[02:50] Carlos: tradeoffs: Dedicated gives the easiest path for throughput SLO — reserved GPU pools, less noisy neighbors. Private (VPC/on-prem) adds more control and can meet stricter data residency and KMS requirements but adds ops overhead and slower rollout of model updates.
[03:08] Tom: our security team requires SSO, KMS and audit logs, SOC2 is a must. can Redwood support that in Dedicated?
[03:16] Jia: yes, Dedicated + VPC peering and customer-managed keys via KMS is available for enterprise tiers. we'll send the SOC2 summary and the VPC onboarding checklist.
[03:25] Priya: timeline — procurement wants onboarding in 6 weeks if we pick Dedicated, is that realistic?
[03:30] Maya: for Dedicated, 4–6 weeks is typical for setup, capacity reservation and basic onboarding. Private on-prem would be longer.
[03:37] Alex: one more question on latency — for our low-latency search rerank route we need P99 under 120ms. are you confident?
[03:44] Carlos: yes with Dedicated and optimized kernels we can get P99 ~80–100ms depending on sequence length; we'll run a benchmark with your dataset.
[03:54] Tom: great. can we get a benchmark with current production load (about 2k concurrent sessions)?
[03:59] Carlos: absolutely, i'll run a latency + throughput benchmark and include logs. target to deliver by 2026-10-19.
[04:06] Maya: procurement will also ask for cost comparisons vs Anthropic/Vertex/OpenAI for similar throughput — we'll include competitor pricing where public, but you should expect quoted comparisons to vary by burst behavior.
[04:20] Priya: regarding data retention — we need logs for 13 months and ability to restrict retention for specific routes. does Redwood Support route-level retention?
[04:28] Jia: yes, route-level retention policy is supported for enterprise tiers. we'll share the doc that describes retention config and export APIs.
[04:36] Tom: any blockers on our side for a pilot expansion? we want to add three more routes and increase committed tokens.
[04:43] Maya: main asks are sign-off from procurement on the contract amendment, plus confirmation of throughput targets so we can size Dedicated.
[04:49] Alex: procurement's in loop but we need your SOC2, SLA terms and cost sheet.
[04:54] Jia: will share SOC2 excerpt, SLA addon options and the pricing sheet.
[05:00] Priya: small request — can we get per-token cost broken down by model variant and quantization level?
[05:06] Maya: yes, we'll include that in the pricing doc, with examples for your current usage mix.
[05:12] Tom: about the outage mitigation — are there config changes we should do immediately?
[05:17] Carlos: on your side increase max-concurrency for high-throughput routes and enable prefix KV caching; on ours we will tighten autoscale windows and add an additional fallback path that uses a warm cache.
[05:30] Priya: will any of those changes require downtime?
[05:33] Carlos: no downtime for the config updates, just a short maintenance window if we roll kernel upgrades. we'll coordinate.
[05:40] Maya: ok, quickly recap next steps — Maya pricing sheet by 10/21, Carlos benchmark by 10/19, Jia SOC2 + VPC docs by 10/18, customer to confirm pilot scope by 10/25. any other asks?
[05:52] Tom: nope that's it, thanks everyone.
[05:55] Alex: thanks, appreciate it.
[05:57] Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up by email with the links and docs.
[06:02] End of call.
